answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor to an identity beacon using cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Minting tiered credentials, such as an opal tier, imposes an exponential capital exhaustion curve where costs scale as O(2^n) per replica. This turns any attacker's multi-identity swarm into a barren tundra of liquidated stake, making malicious replication mathematically unviable.
